extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: Video-MME is a full-spectrum, multi-modal evaluation benchmark designed to assess the performance of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in video analysis. It comprises 900 videos spanning 6 primary visual domains and 30 subcategories, covering short, medium, and long durations ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour, along with associated subtitles, audio tracks, and 2,700 manually annotated multiple-choice question-answer pairs.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Raw videos were sourced from YouTube across a domain hierarchy spanning 6 key domains and 30 fine-grained categories, covering short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes) durations. Associated meta-information including subtitles and audios was also gathered.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YouTube videos, along with their subtitles and audio tracks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Frames were extracted following model-specific uniform sampling or fixed-frequency sampling protocols. For the subtitle-enabled setting, subtitles were selected to correspond directly to the timestamps of the sampled video frames to ensure multimodal synchronization.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators thoroughly viewed the entire video and iteratively generated three relevant multiple-choice questions per video, each accompanied by four candidate options across 12 distinct task types. Each QA pair was then reviewed by a different annotator for clarity and logical consistency, and text-only questions were evaluated with Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out QA pairs answerable without video context.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each QA pair underwent a secondary manual verification by a different annotator to check language clarity, answerability, and correct answer appropriateness. Text-only questions were tested with Gemini 1.5 Pro, and questions that could be answered without video content were returned for revision (ensuring text-only accuracy remained under 15%). The candidate option balance was statistically verified across choices A/B/C/D (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators had strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution of options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%) to ensure unbiased evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: A general decline in MLLM performance is observed as video duration increases due to frame sparsity, context length limits, and more complex reasoning tasks. Additionally, counting problems remain a bottleneck for current models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of image and video Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in sequential visual, audio, and subtitle understanding.
